steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: A land of eternity without suffering... The ultimate hope for the future, spoken of in ancient legends.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But nobody could have foreseen that when we gazed upon the border of the universe, we would realize asking for a future was the unreasonable part of the demand.

spans.text: But nobody could have foreseen that when we gazed upon the border of the universe, we would realize asking for
future was the unreasonable part of the demand.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}... The you you are now, the you who has seen the devastation plaguing this planet for yourself—

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: What sort of future do you still hope for?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: PRTS's functionality is limited, the PCS system is completely destroyed, and DWDB-221E is also lost... There are not many tools we can use left.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Did you expect things to turn out this way?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Friston, Ed, Lu...

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I cherish the time we worked together. I was greatly looking forward to seeing what hopeful answers you could find.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But it is a shame. Time has shown just how futile your efforts were, how fruitless they turned out... though they are still worthy of respect.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: ...How I regret that things have come to this.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Allow me to borrow your legacy one last time. My plans for the future never did obtain your complete approval, but at the very least, we can still have a future.

spans.text: Allow me to borrow your legacy one last time. My plans for the future never did obtain your complete approval, but at the very least, we can still

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Perhaps, in this future, we shall meet again.
It is the deep of night.
Amiya silently sits on the edge of her bed, unable to sleep.
The room is brand-new, the air exceedingly fresh.
The narrow space is laid out almost exactly the same as its original. She has no need to change any of her minute, unconscious habits that have built up over the years.
But ever since she moved in, she has not enjoyed a good night's sleep.
A faint sigh.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Amiya...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa? No, I wasn't calling for you...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...Did... Did you hear me earlier?

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: I live in your consciousness, Amiya. There is no need for you to lie to yourself.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: It is rather late. Shouldn't you be asleep?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Mon3tr and Closure, they're... They're doing the last bit of theory-testing before we bring back Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There's nothing I can do to help directly, but I also can't get any rest like this... Though I did promise the Doctor I would.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: I am always around if you need to get things off your chest, Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I know everyone's working their hardest to bring Dr. Kal'tsit back. I need to stay strong too.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's a strange feeling. The day the incident happened, I thought we had lost her forever.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But then Mon3tr appeared, and she told us there was still a possibility of bringing her back, a sliver of hope...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It feels just like... that first time in the ruins of Londinium... when I saw Theresa.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I still remember it clearly. What I felt at the time was certainly not joy...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm sorry, Theresa.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: It's alright, Amiya.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: We have already said our farewells to Theresa, have we not?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Right...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm not too sure, and I dare not believe... If we really do manage to 'bring back' Dr. Kal'tsit, will the person who returns be her?

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: You should know, Amiya, that Kal'tsit is different from everyone else.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Mon3tr said Kal'tsit has been through this sort of thing before.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Perhaps what we consider a miracle truly can come to pass?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But after all our time together, Dr. Kal'tsit's basically a part of my family. I can't even imagine how she could be any different from us.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa, can you tell me one of your stories about you and her? From long ago.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I want to know what sort of person she is in your eyes.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: I can only tell you about the memories Theresa has of Kal'tsit, Amiya. I am unqualified to tell you a story in her stead.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: I do not believe that is what you want, either.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You're right. Maybe... Maybe I just want to hear Dr. Kal'tsit's voice again...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: She's taken care of me for so long, and taught me so much... but when I think about it, I know very little about her.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I had so many questions I wanted to ask her and Theresa... but they were all such serious questions. I couldn't give them any more burdens to bear.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Maybe... when they thought the time was right, they would've told me of their own accord.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But the right time never came.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: I understand. Theresa and Kal'tsit were both very important to you.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: You do not need to hide your emotions from me, Amiya, nor should you bear everything alone. Go and tell Closure and Mon3tr, and the Doctor.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: No matter how things may turn out, you should not leave behind any regrets, alright?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You're right... I'll be fine, Theresa. Once I step out of this room, I'll be back to normal.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Don't worry. No matter what comes to pass, I won't let Closure and Mon3tr see any dismay on my face.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: But I cannot help but worry about you, Amiya.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: You have had far less sleep than usual this past month. You must get more rest.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: You should also be aware that ever since you used the Black Crown's power in Ursus, your vital signs have all been very abnormal.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: Not only that, but you have been avoiding routine Rhodes Island medical checkups ever since Kal'tsit left us.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I can also tell that... some changes started even before that.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: When the Doctor and I were exploring Civilight Eterna, we discovered a model from the Slumber Bridge project, and borrowed its power to fight Priestess.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I don't fully understand it yet, but I can sense that this model seems to have linked me even closer to the Black Crown.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I can use the power of the Lord of Fiends more easily, I can sense emotions more intensely. Sometimes, I can even hear voices, and I can't shut them out.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's like... I'm back to before Dr. Kal'tsit gave me these rings.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: I am detecting that the connection between you and the Black Crown is deepening at a rapid pace. This is unprecedented in the entire line of the Kings of Sarkaz.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: I cannot explain its cause, but it is not something to take lightly, no matter what it may be.

steps.name: Civilight Eterna
steps.text: You must take care, Amiya. I believe you should let the Doctor know as soon as possible.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Right... I understand.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I promise I'll pay close attention to my condition, but is it okay if we don't tell the Doctor right now?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Was that Closure's workstation?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Have they finally gotten results...?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Alright, after squashing I-don't-know how many bugs, I can finally say with certainty that there's no problems in the entire dataset.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Here goes! I'm praying this is the last simulation we have to run!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: This time, it'll be a success...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Aye dun dink dere'll be enny broblems et al—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hey, Mon3tr, don't move, or the data cables on your head will fall off!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Keep her still, Warfarin, then help me inspect the simulation life pod's cables, make sure they're all connected properly.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Alright, alright...

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: You seriously think I understand any of this...? Never had to deal with this sort of stuff in Medical.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Look, I had to start from scratch too when I was studying all that data from Mon3tr! Forget it, all systems green here, no need to check!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Alright, everyone ready?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Here goes—
One minute, two minutes... Ten minutes pass, each one an eternity longer than the last, all without any warning pop-ups or worrying flashes of red.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Cmoncmoncmoncmon—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Don't...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (Deep breath)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: No, it will make it!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: This is all based on reasonable assumptions and a carefully calculated foundation, and it's in accordance with that 'life-phase transition' stuff she was going on about, so even if all we can get is a glimmer...

spans.text: This is all based on reasonable assumptions and a carefully calculated foundation,
it's in accordance with that 'life-phase transition' stuff she was going on about, so even if all we can get is a glimmer...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: ...Even if all we can see is a glimmer of hope, I'll be happy.

spans.text: is a glimmer of hope, I'll be happy.

steps.text: The Vampire's red eyes stare at the monitor, unblinking. The fluorescence reflects off Closure's pale face as a series of pinpricks of light, the process's various readings constantly in flux.
The progress bar on the monitor stops, just as it is about to reach the end.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: ...Working?
Failure. Again.
After so many failures, she should already have gotten used to seeing this result, yet defeat still weighs heavy on her heart.
Closure looks towards the scarlet glare, subconsciously trying to use the naked eye to pick out the true cause of the issue from the morass of data.

But what made her despair the most was the fact that she had checked over every key snippet of code countless times over. If every step was performed correctly, but still didn't result in success, then doesn't that mean...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Where's the problem this time? This shouldn't be happening—

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Don't look so glum.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Nobody's done bioengineering this complicated before. We must've missed a spot somewhere.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Calm down, keep looking, and you'll definitely find it.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I know, I'm not giving up yet.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Drone No. 6, begin recording progress reports 1860 to 1864.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Project: Sarcophagus Resurrection Experiment. Progress: 0.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: But why...?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Our last two attempts should've succeeded. Even if Kal'tsit severed the connection between us, there are other methods we can theoretically use to replace the gemini cycle's information transmission function.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I stored all the memories Kal'tsit encoded as energy strings inside. Every single one of the Sarcophagus's parameters is correct.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Using 'Oka', blank Originium, as the base of Kal'tsit's reconstructed body is theoretically feasible...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: But where's the issue? What are we missing...?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Maybe...
The same thought floats through everyone's minds, but none of them dare say it out loud.

options: Maybe what we're missing is...
The part that makes Kal'tsit Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Doctor? You're here!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Sorry, we couldn't—

options: It's alright. We expected to run into difficulties.
Though this outcome is a little disappointing.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Don't... Don't lose heart just yet, Doctor!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Rhodes Island's best engineer hasn't given up! With Terra's genius hacker on your side, making sense of the data Kal'tsit left behind is a done deal! On the honor of my spot in the Kazdel's Elite 100—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I will find a way to bring Kal'tsit back!

spans.text: find a way to bring Kal'tsit back!

options: If that's how you feel, I've got nothing to worry about.
Wasn't I meant to be the one giving the pep talk?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I mean, you did look a little disappointed just now.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I promised Kal'tsit I wouldn't let you or Amiya handle all the pressure by yourselves anymore.

options: Thank you, Closure.
Rhodes Island still needs Kal'tsit.
We're all hoping she can come back to us.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Yeah!

options: By the way, news from Ursus.
Crownslayer found more clues about the Sarcophagus.
It's time to set off again.
Maybe once we actually find it...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: You see... This w-wounded joint... If you... set it like this... It won't hurt.

steps.name: Haggard Infected
steps.text: Spasibo, Vetochki! I'm feeling better already!

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I learned... it from Rhodes... Island's d-doctors.

steps.name: Haggard Infected
steps.text: Speaking of, this Deity Grypherburg place sure is something, having stoves like these we can warm ourselves with. No wonder those nobles can sit pretty in the cities without caring about winter.

steps.name: Haggard Infected
steps.text: Can we really settle down here, Vetochki?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: It's... okay. Raidian said sh-she'd protect us.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Now... we don't... need to be afraid.
Good grief, it's absolutely freezing here...
Can't you add a little more firewood—My apologies. What I meant to say is, if you are still lacking in firewood, I will be happy to help.

steps.name: Haggard Infected
steps.text: Is she... Imperial Guard? What're the Imperial Guard doing here?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: D-Don't be scared!

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: She... Sh-She helped us before... Don't you remember?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Thank you, Vetochki. Thank you for speaking up for me, and thank you for remembering me.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: *sigh*... And after we forged a friendship in the fires of egress, too. I think my heart's beginning to break.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: You only have your conspicuous uniform to blame, 'Sergeant'.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I'm terribly sorry, but I am no lord with the time to change outfits for every single errand. I need this uniform as my free pass through other parts of Grypherburg.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It's been a while since I last dropped by to say hello. Everything still going smoothly? How are your medicine stocks?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Hmm, our other supplies are just barely enough, but you know it's nearly impossible to obtain anti-Oripathy medication in the capital, and we're too far from our headquarters to transport more here.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: If it wasn't for the matter of the Originium vein, the construction of Grypherburg's Oripathy medicine production line would've been on the agenda.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Who would have thought...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Well, whatever the case, thank you for offering us this shelter.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I did make a promise. And it is simply an idle factory owned by my family. Even then, it still can't fit everyone inside... It is far too cold here.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Although the paperwork to shelter the Infected has been sorted out, now is not a good time for any of you to wander about the city.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I regret to say that... as things stand, I have no way of offering you better conditions.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I know they're only allowed to stay in Grypherburg as key witnesses to the tragedy of the Far North... even though this trial has not yet manifested itself.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: This does not change the fact that there is nowhere in this nation for them.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...That may change, sooner than you think.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Sorry, did you say something?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: No, nothing. Let's shelve this discussion for later. I came to Rhodes Island today for another matter.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Where is that 'Doctor' of yours right now?

options: Zelgrad?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Yep. Based on your team's intelligence, we can assume Ursus is secretly researching the Sarcophagus somewhere near Grypherburg.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: And according to Crownslayer's info, we've found a few clues that can validate this assumption.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Despite Ursus's critical Originium shortage, there's a delivery of vast amounts of Originium from the city to the outskirts, same time, every day. Always in the same direction.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Their Originium logistics channels are well-hidden, and it's a bad idea for us to chase them too closely. But we've checked all the satellite cities around the capital, and none of them have the sort of industry that needs this much Originium.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: None except the satellite city where the First Army is stationed. Zelgrad.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: But the moment any lead we have points here, it's cut off. Guess Grypherburg is putting a lot of effort into hiding the flow of energy.

options: Nobody's mentioned this city to us during our time in Grypherburg.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: You're not the only ones in the dark. Most Ursines are barely even aware Zelgrad exists.

options: Ursus must have a good reason to keep a secret like that.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: We can also assume that, if large quantities of Originium go missing at a time like this, there's probably industry magnates who aren't too happy about it.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: What's more, the Fourth Army's pretty much at the gates. They definitely have spies watching every move happening in Grypherburg.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: But that's the reason why one thing really stands out.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Zelgrad is supposed to be a closed-off special district, but it's recently been advertising itself as 'a safe haven for the Infected'.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Their public statement is that the First Army firmly denounces the tragedy that happened in the Far Northern mines, so they are willing to shelter those Infected who lost their homes during the unrest.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: 'As a show of the absolute kindness the tsar has for the Infected.'

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Naturally, the first reaction everyone had on hearing this news was suspicion. We've been unable to get any information about any Infected who enter Zelgrad.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: We've also found some issues with the records Crownslayer found in the district gates. Once you factor out the outsourced materials being used as cover, imports of pharmaceutical products and raw materials are almost nil.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: None of this is concrete evidence, though. If we really want to know the truth, I'm afraid our only choice is an on-site inspection.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: That's all the clues my side can offer you at the moment. We'll keep up our work at the edges of Grypherburg, and get as much information as we can into your hands.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Oh, right. Don't forget to tell the little USSG cubs what good work they've done next time you see them, Doctor.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Not just for their information-gathering skills. They were amazing during the recent crisis in Grypherburg. They're all bona-fide, grown-up Rhodes Island operators now.

options: I will. Everyone did great.
You're all the best of Rhodes Island's operators.
Thank you, Dur-nar.
Remember to tell Zima and her crew to stay safe.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Kal'tsit sealed away the Sarcophagus's core when she was in Chernobog. Theoretically speaking, Ursus's current technological know-how isn't enough for them to restart it.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: What's stranger is, shouldn't Ursus be trying to turn it into an energy source at a time like this? Why do the opposite and consume tons of Originium? What are they actually trying to do?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, what I'm most worried about is Zelgrad accepting the Infected.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I know this isn't a rational assessment, but... I find it very hard to believe the First Army is letting them in out of the goodness of their hearts.

options: An incredibly suspicious act.
Our top priority is gathering even more intelligence about Zelgrad.
Closure...?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What are you doing, Closure?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ah, sorry, just a sec, nearly done. Let's see what secrets this website is hiding.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Wait... Are you hacking into an Ursine government website?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Nonono, no hacking involved. The site I'm looking at is the 'Ursus State Council Executive Department Website'. The service-level news is for the public.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Government news, Catastrophe warnings... Ah, there it is, Zelgrad's notice saying they'll shelter Infected. Man, too many network fluctuations, filtering and download speeds are real slow.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But what's obvious is that a lot of this is just fake news to keep up with appearances.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Check this city migration schedule, for example. If this info is true, it means there's been three nomadic city collisions near Grypherburg just last month!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: This sort of forgery definitely means they're hiding something. Just need to dig a little deeper...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Are you sure you're not crossing a line here, Closure?

spans.text: you're not crossing a line here, Closure?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm not! Well... Maybe a little?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But whoever kludged together this website clearly isn't very good at network security. The website's server is directly connected to their internal database.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Nothing too important in here, all just basic info on city routes. But Zelgrad's urban identification code is in here, as well as their public logistics and transportation records.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Okay, give me three minutes, and ZOOT will calculate the optimal route from Grypherburg to Zelgrad.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I won't leave any tracks behind, guaranteed!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: But all we have is a lock on the satellite city's position. How are we meant to get in?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: A direct attack? I don't have any issues with that, honestly...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If the Sarcophagus is in the hands of the First Army, that means it'll be heavily guarded. A direct attack is out of the question.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, I'm wondering if we can take advantage of Zelgrad admitting Infected—

options: A heads-up from Raidian—
Take care. Looks like someone's here.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Raidian... and Lieutenant Gorchekova?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I happened to run into her. She says she has something to discuss with the Doctor, face-to-face.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It's been quite a while, my friends.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Though I do not believe I have met you before, Gospozha... Vampire?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Y'know, it's been so long since anyone's mentioned it that I practically forgot I am a Vampire.

spans.text: Y'know, it's been so long since anyone's mentioned it that I practically forgot I

options: Her name is Closure.
She's an amazing engineer.
She's an amazing hacker.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It is my honor to meet you, Gospozha Closure.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It is clear that you are an excellent... Hmm...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hmm...?
Eloysius turns to Raidian, choosing to communicate using sign language.
'Is this place safe?'

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I don't detect any signals of dubious origin. Closure can also guarantee we are free to speak here.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wha? Sorry, I don't understand sign language—

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Everything here was wired by us, correct?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Yeah?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: (Quietly) Does this mean nobody is monitoring us right now...?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Oh, definitely not. You don't have to worry about that sort of thing when I'm here.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Just act like you're back on the ship—err, back at HQ. You're welcome, by the way.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Spasibo. Then let us get down to brass tacks. Our last discussion ended on the topic of the Sarcophagus's whereabouts.

spans.text: . Then let us get down to brass tacks. Our last discussion ended on the topic of the Sarcophagus's whereabouts.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: In regards to intelligence on the matter, I have made some... not-so-small headway.

options: Thank you for being willing to share it with us.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Yet another promise of mine. All part of our cooperative agreement.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Besides, even if I did not share this information with you, I'm sure you would already be trying all sorts of ways to get into Zelgrad, as is typical for you Rhodes Islanders.

options: We will abide by the laws of Deity Grypherburg.
I assure you, we won't do anything illegal.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Eep..!
A beep on the terminal draws Amiya's attention as the Vampire instinctively covers the screen. The young Imperial Guardswoman looks, but makes no comment.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Very well. I know full well just how difficult it is to establish a relationship built upon trust.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: But I insist on recommending Rhodes Island secure a legitimate status for your operations... for there will be many bumps on the road ahead.
She's right. Rhodes Island must be well-prepared.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Are you... General Khratov?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Just Hellagur is fine.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: According to the Doctor's instructions, I have attempted to contact, and succeeded in contacting a Vice Chairman of the State Council, Vasily Gorchikov.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: In Grypherburg's eyes, Rhodes Island is on sound legal footing.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: So it was your idea all along. I was wondering why...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Wait, how did you know he would be able to meet with the vice chairman—with Father?

options: It's simple. Because we could.
It was Operator Hellagur who suggested it in the first place.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It seems I have been underestimating the intelligence and contacts Rhodes Island has access to this whole time...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: If that's the case, I have no more worries. Allow me to formally pass on this invitation to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: An invitation from His Imperial Majesty Fyodor Vladimirovich.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: This is why I have come here today. Now, allow me to escort you to the audience chamber.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: You're here.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Do your clothes fit? Come closer, and let me see.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Hmm. At least they fit you better than your old clothes.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: Thank you. They fit fine, and they're comfortable.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: You are my guest. This is the least of what I can provide you. If there is anything else you need, please do not hesitate to ask my adjutant.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: How is Anatoliy, Yasha?

steps.name: Diligent Servant
steps.text: The Generalik is currently choosing his retinue for the next operation.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: He simply cannot wait, can he? Remind him to pick strong young recruits, no more wily old soldiers.

steps.name: Diligent Servant
steps.text: I already have, ma'am.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Very good.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: What is your name? I cannot be calling you 'child' the entire time.

steps.name: Cautus
steps.text: Hierda. I'm called Hierda, ma'am.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Well then, young Hierda.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: As I must remain here to maintain discipline, I need you to accompany my son to Zelgrad as his 'doctor'.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: He is going there to patrol, and look after the city. In turn, I hope you can look after him.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: You should know that Ursus has recently run into misfortune. The unrest continues to spread unabated, and the number of people who want him dead rivals the number who want to snatch my authority away from me.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: I want you to stay by his side and protect him, and once all the dust has settled, bring him back to me safe and sound.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...'Once all the dust has settled'?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: You need only reply. Can you do this?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I need to know where my companions are first, and if they are safe.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: How careless of me. I forgot to tell you that they have already headed onwards.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: 'Onwards'?

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: To Zelgrad. The city is now open to both the public and the Infected. Your companions are the first lucky few to be accepted by this new policy.

steps.name: Svetlana
steps.text: Once you go there, you may meet with them.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...What's this?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I'm sure I was here earlier, but he's not here.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: (This ship is too large. Where am I supposed to find the young general?)

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Faint Voice
steps.text: ...drat...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Ah, someone's there.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Hello, may I ask—

steps.name: Enraged Officer
steps.text: ...Everyone knows being one of his bodyguards is a death sentence. Who's still willing to go?

steps.name: Enraged Officer
steps.text: And now he's actually managed to figure out he just needs to pick some nobody greenhorns who don't know what they're getting into—

steps.name: Enraged Officer
steps.text: How shameless!

steps.name: Determined Officer
steps.text: (Quietly) Shh, keep it down! Let's talk somewhere else, I know where we can avoid the cameras.

steps.name: Enraged Officer
steps.text: I had to let it all out today.

steps.name: Determined Officer
steps.text: (Quietly) I get it, I get it, bratan. This is why we need to keep getting our people into his personal guard, even if it means sending them to the slaughterhouse.

spans.text: (Quietly) I get it, I get it,
. This is why we need to keep getting our people into his personal guard, even if it means sending them to the slaughterhouse.

steps.name: Determined Officer
steps.text: (Quietly) The marshal's clearly lost her ability to judge the situation. She thinks that with the new weapon, we can sleep peacefully at night, but she doesn't know the real problem was on the inside all along.

steps.name: Determined Officer
steps.text: (Quietly) Letting a useless boy play toy soldiers with the army just to earn some cheap glory, waving a live blade around like it's an emperor's scepter!

steps.name: Determined Officer
steps.text: (Quietly) She even lets him randomly execute the men without penalty... It's absolutely ridiculous.

steps.name: Enraged Officer
steps.text: She keeps going on about how we have to do it for Ursus, but today's killing was certainly not for Ursus!

steps.name: Determined Officer
steps.text: (Quietly) And if things keep going on like this, how're we supposed to deal with rebels? There was a Corporal Andrei in my barracks, all he did was follow the Marshal's orders to stop him, and he got his throat slashed open for it.

steps.name: Determined Officer
steps.text: (Quietly) Andrei wasn't even part of that 'Death Squad'. I had a look at his corpse, his eyes wide open, just a kid with a confused look on his face under the mortician's sheet...

steps.name: Enraged Officer
steps.text: We've got to do something already!

steps.name: Determined Officer
steps.text: (Quietly) You're right...

steps.name: Determined Officer
steps.text: We need to act.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: 'Act'?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: What do they mean by...?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Act?
